record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
record.context_brief: Reverse Shannon theorem for entanglement-assisted coding
record.original_question: For quantum channels S and T, define CE(T,S) as an entanglement-assisted asymptotic simulation capacity: the supremum of rates r for which many parallel copies of one channel can simulate many copies of the other using arbitrary coding, decoding, and any needed shared entanglement with vanishing error. Is entanglement-assisted coding reversible for all channel pairs, in the sense that CE(T,S) equals the reciprocal of CE(S,T)?

evidence.quote:
For any two quantum channels S and T , define the entanglement assisted capacity CE(T, S) of T for S-messages as the supremum of all rates r such that, for large n, rn parallel copies of T may be simulated by n copies of S, where the simulation involves arbitrary coding and decoding operations using (if necessary) arbitrarily many entangled pairs between sender and receiver, and where the errors go to zero as n → ∞.
Show that CE(T, S) = CE(S, T )−1.
The problem is solved for the special case of a known “tensor power source”, i. e. a source emitting the same, known, density matrix at each time step.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let S and T be quantum channels (completely positive trace-preserving maps between finite-dimensional matrix algebras). Define the entanglement-assisted asymptotic simulation capacity C_E(T, S) as the supremum of all real numbers r ≥ 0 such that, for every ε > 0 and all sufficiently large n, there exist encoding and decoding quantum operations E_n and D_n, together with a (possibly arbitrarily large) shared entangled state between sender and receiver, such that the composite map D_n ∘ S^{⊗n} ∘ E_n (acting with the help of the shared entanglement) simulates T^{⊗⌊rn⌋} to within diamond-norm error at most ε. Prove or disprove: for every pair of quantum channels S and T (with C_E(S,T) > 0),
            C_E(T, S) = 1 / C_E(S, T).
That is, show that entanglement-assisted asymptotic channel simulation is reversible for all pairs of channels.
artifact.status_search_result: The Quantum Reverse Shannon Theorem, which implies the reversibility C_E(T,S) = 1/C_E(S,T) via the formula C_E(T,S) = C_E(T)/C_E(S) where C_E is the entanglement-assisted classical capacity, was established by Bennett, Devetak, Harrow, Shor, and Winter (arXiv:0912.5537, published 2014) and independently by Berta, Christandl, and Renner (Comm. Math. Phys., 2011). Thus the problem is solved.

status_evidence.title: Quantum Reverse Shannon Theorem
status_evidence.snippet: Bennett, Devetak, Harrow, Shor, Winter prove that any quantum channel can be simulated using shared entanglement and classical communication at rate equal to entanglement-assisted capacity.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the entanglement-assisted reverse Shannon theorem implying reversibility of simulation.

status_evidence.title: The Quantum Reverse Shannon Theorem Based on One-Shot Information Theory
status_evidence.snippet: Berta, Christandl, Renner give an alternative proof of the quantum reverse Shannon theorem.
status_evidence.claim: Independent proof confirming the reversibility result.
